analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts: scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. The head version adds per-shard route lanes (test-provider-1 through test-provider-5), a SHARDED set, and helpers matrix_shards, job_lanes and requested_lanes. test-provider-ci-workflow.py adds PROVIDER_SHARDS plus assertions that each shard reads its own lane and requests count 1.

I found no runtime provider, coordinator or native-runtime code changes, so the provider threat-model assets and boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and others) are not touched.

The security-relevant controls these tests pin are preserved or strengthened:
- Fork PRs never contact the plane.
- Only an exact label array is accepted.
- TLS verification stays on.
- Plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown.
- Routed jobs keep read-only permissions, no id-token, and timeouts of 60 minutes or less.
- Release and credentialed workflows keep literal runners.

The shard change only alters how many lanes are requested. Each shard gets an independent lane, and the test still checks a fallback for every requested lane, so no new attack surface appears.

The patch is a test-only change. It verifies the workflow YAML (ci.yml), which is not supplied here, so the actual workflow edits were not reviewed and the tests assert expectations I cannot confirm against that file. Those workflow edits, and the plane's handling of the new lane names, are the remaining integration questions.
